known_incidents.note: Upstream release notes identify 5.6.1 as vulnerable and 5.6.2 as the fix.

candidates.maintenance: Active; v6.0.0 was released in July 2026.
candidates.runtime_footprint: Zero runtime dependencies and Node-only by policy; never included in the browser bundle.
candidates.testability: A focused CLI fixture can exercise color-enabled, color-disabled, FORCE_COLOR, and non-interactive output.
security_notes: Upstream identified v5.6.1 as vulnerable and released v5.6.2 as the fix; exact reviewed versions and frozen lockfiles are required.
candidates.outcome: Readable styled terminal diagnostics for an explicit Node CLI capability.
native_alternatives: Minimal ANSI escape sequences owned by the CLI when the use case stays trivial
candidates.adoption_guard: Do not install by default. Add only when a generated Node CLI actually needs styled TTY output and a focused fixture proves color, no-color, and non-interactive behavior.
candidates.replacement_or_removal: Remove when the consuming CLI no longer needs styled output or a smaller platform/project-owned implementation fully covers the accepted use case.
evidence: Chalk 6.0.0 is ESM, requires Node >=22, is MIT licensed, and declares zero runtime dependencies.
The v5.6.2 release notes explicitly fix the vulnerability introduced in v5.6.1.

candidates.maintenance: Mature but low-change; npm 0.5.21 was published in 2021 and the latest upstream commit observed in this review is from November 2022.
candidates.runtime_footprint: Approximately 85 kB package footprint plus two runtime dependencies; duplicates native Node behavior for the supported modern baseline.
candidates.testability: Use a transpiled-stack fixture with node --enable-source-maps; any exception must first reproduce a native Node gap.
native_alternatives: node:module module.setSourceMapsSupport() when programmatic control is required
candidates.adoption_guard: Do not add to the React/Vite baseline. Re-open only for a demonstrated modern-Node compatibility gap such as a required vm.runInThisContext path that native source-map support cannot cover.
candidates.replacement_or_removal: Not applicable while rejected; any exception must be removed once the demonstrated native Node gap is eliminated.
evidence: Upstream documents that Node >=12.12.0 normally no longer requires this package because --enable-source-maps is built in.
Modern Node also exposes module.setSourceMapsSupport(); the CLI flag remains the preferred early-process path.

candidates.maintenance: Stable legacy wrapper; v2.0.2 was released in 2018 and the latest upstream change observed in this review was a typings fix in January 2024.
candidates.runtime_footprint: Zero runtime dependencies, but still adds browser code and an abstraction layer for functionality already provided by the platform.
candidates.testability: A browser or DOM fixture can exercise document.visibilityState, document.hidden, and visibilitychange directly; a React hook can be tested without the wrapper.
candidates.outcome: React/browser behavior that reacts to a page becoming visible or hidden.
native_alternatives: A small project-owned React hook when component ergonomics require one
candidates.adoption_guard: Do not add to modern browser bundles. Re-open only if the supported-browser policy intentionally includes a browser without the standard Page Visibility API.
candidates.replacement_or_removal: Not applicable while rejected; prefer deleting any compatibility wrapper once the supported browser floor makes it unnecessary.
evidence: MDN classifies the Page Visibility API as Baseline Widely available and available across browsers since July 2015.
Visibility.js 2.0.2 is a wrapper/polyfill-era package; its latest repository change after the 2018 release was a typings fix in 2024.
